title: GPU memory management
subtitle: ActiveKV inverts who owns memory: history in pinned host RAM, the GPU a budgeted working set.

lede: ActiveKV began with a constraint I did not accept. Stock vLLM keeps a request's whole key-value cache on the GPU, so on a 32 GB Intel Arc Pro GPU the card decides how much context a model can hold. I inverted who owns memory and gave the device a stated budget, so the operator chooses the trade-off. I give GPU memory owners, budgets and lifetimes, on two vendors' hardware. The device side is one arena shared by every dense layer: staging pages for 32K-token tiles plus a pool of pages. Each context has a target it holds by right, a burst it may borrow while pages are free, and a floor it needs to run.
quote: Memory is a design decision, not a default.
evidence: KV-cache offload for LLM inference: pinned host memory as the copy of record and the GPU as a budgeted page arena, with 2 GiB of host memory per 32K-token history.
Latency engineering under concurrency: reclaimed device memory spent to cut inter-token latency from 273.58 to 141.48 ms on long prompts with four concurrent requests.
GPU memory management: staging leases released only on completed fences, quarantine on an unknown fence outcome, and a host-pool fit that prints its own formula.
TensorRT and TensorRT-LLM engineering: a throughput runtime with 0 CUDA allocations after the first second of a trace, down from about 4,200.
author: Corey James
